title: Every finding in the City’s grant audits since 2015
question: What exactly did the auditor find, how serious was it, and was it fixed by the next year?
finding: 11 findings in 11 years. 2 were rated a material weakness: 2016-002 (Special Tests and Provision: Maximum Per-Unit Subsidy and Underwriting Requirements); 2020-002 (Period of Performance). The heading that recurs most is “Procurement and Suspension and Debarment”: findings in fiscal 2015 and 2016, after one under the same heading the year before (2014-004), about different programmes (Port Security Grant Program; Assistance to Firefighters Grant). The following year’s report said corrective action had been taken on 11 of the 11 findings it followed up. 1 finding was a repeat (2015-001, repeating a fiscal 2014 finding the report said had not been fixed). 3 findings give dollar figures under the “questioned costs” heading; the rest say there were none or leave it blank.
how: Each finding numbered for the year in the single audit’s schedule of findings: its heading, whether it sits under the City’s accounts or under federal grants, the grade the auditor gave it, the federal programme, the first sentence under “Questioned Costs”, and what the following year’s report says about corrective action. “Same heading before” lists earlier findings with an identical heading, including fiscal 2014 findings named in the 2015 report.
limits: Headings are broad categories from federal audit rules (for example “Reporting”), so the same heading in two years can concern different departments and programmes; it does not by itself mean an unfixed problem. “Fixed” is the status the City and its auditor reported the following year. The questioned-cost text is the report’s own first sentence, cut short; read the page for the full amount and context. This project’s other audit screen counts grant findings from the federal audit database from 2019; it does not include findings on the City’s accounts, so its count for fiscal 2020 is one lower than here. The fiscal 2020 single audit answers “No” to whether any federal-grant findings had to be reported, yet its schedule lists finding 2020-002; the summary line looks wrong, and the finding is counted here.

rows.severity: Significant Deficiency in Internal Control over Compliance

rows.about: Internal Controls Over Evaluation of Credit Balances

rows.program: Disaster Grants – Public Assistance (Presidentially Declared Disasters)
rows.questioned: The City adjusted its schedule of expenditures of federal awards to correct for the issues identified above. Thus there were no resulting questioned costs reported.

rows.about: Reliability of System-Generated Reports used for Financial Reporting
rows.severity: Significant Deficiency in Internal Controls over Financial Reporting

rows.questioned: The population of expenditures subject to the procurement requirement in fiscal year 2015-16 included 4 contractors with total expenditures of $1,007,920. We selected the two contractors with the highest expenditure amounts, which covered $897,868 of the population.

rows.about: Special Tests and Provision: Maximum Per-Unit Subsidy and Underwriting Requirements
rows.questioned: The project included HOME funds of $8,134,000, which exceeded the maximum per-unit subsidy of $6,976,330 by $1,157,670.

rows.repeat: Yes: last year’s finding under this heading was not yet fixed

rows.about: Activities Allowed or Unallowed; Allowable Costs/Cost Principles
rows.questioned: We selected 2 of the 4 quarterly time studies for testing. The identified errors resulted in an understatement of $6,777 in federal reimbursements.
